name: UltraTech Cement Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest cement producer (Aditya Birla group; Grasim holds ~56%, model knowledge) with the broadest pan-India grey-cement, white-cement and RMC network plus overseas plants; acquired India Cements (model knowledge). Q2 FY27: sales Rs23,295 cr (+19%), EBITDA Rs3,719 cr (OPM 16%), PAT Rs1,501 cr (+21%). Targets 240 MT capacity and EBITDA Rs1,400/t (Sahi, 21 Oct). P/E 40.6, mcap Rs3.6 lakh cr, 12m +3.6%.

revenue_mix.geography: India (pan-India, trade ~65-70% of sales; model knowledge)

revenue_mix.segment: white cement, RMC, building products, overseas

exposures.mechanism: Power & fuel ~25% of costs (model knowledge); costs ~84% of sales. Kiln fuel ~62% of that, ~55% petcoke/imported (UltraTech has high WHRS and green-power share, so lower than Ambuja) -> ~7% of sales exposed. +15% -> +1.1% of sales -> EBITDA -6.8% at 16% OPM; 40% passed through -> -4.0%; EV/MCap 1.04, persistence 0.4 -> -1.7. Empirical F_COAL_INTL +1.29 (t +1.3) has the wrong sign and is treated as noise (cement stocks rallied with rising coal in 2022-23 on price hikes).

evidence.note: Q2: profit +21% to Rs1,494-1,501 cr, revenue +19%, volume-led with efficiency gains; shares fell up to 5% from day's high (Moneycontrol/CNBC TV18/Business Standard); targets 240 MT capacity and Rs1,400 EBITDA/t (Sahi 21 Oct)
Nomura: Rs12-15/bag hikes needed to offset fuel; UltraTech top pick (Moneycontrol 12 Oct); ET 16 Oct: strong Q2 volumes but fuel costs may weigh

exposures.mechanism: Diesel-linked road freight ~10% of costs; +10% Brent -> retail diesel +5% -> costs +0.5% -> EBITDA -2.6% at 16% OPM; 40% pass-through, x1.04 x0.4 -> -0.5; with packaging -> -0.8. Pack shows no significant empirical Brent beta.

Imported fuel ~7% of sales: +3% -> +0.2% of sales -> EBITDA -1.3% at 16% OPM; pass-through and hedges -> -0.4. Overseas operations (UAE, Bahrain, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh; model knowledge) give small USD offset.

+Rs10/bag (~2.5% realisation) -> +2.5/16 = +15.6% EBITDA; x1.04 x persistence 0.4 -> +6.5; shaded to +6.0 as the pack shows UltraTech already carries the 'quality' premium and volume share loss is small.

evidence.note: Nomura: Rs12-15/bag hikes needed to offset fuel; UltraTech top pick (Moneycontrol 12 Oct); ET 16 Oct: strong Q2 volumes but fuel costs may weigh

exposures.mechanism: Housing ~65% of cement demand, elasticity 0.25 -> +10% sales -> +1.6% volume; contribution margin ~55% -> +0.9% of sales = +5.5% EBITDA at 16% OPM; x1.04 x0.5 -> +2.9; shaded for the 7 Oct repo hike.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, stance 'calibrated tightening' (Reuters/The Hindu/Moneycontrol headlines)

exposures.mechanism: UltraTech has the largest infra/institutional (RMC, ready-mix, project-linked) share, ~30-35% of volume. +10% capex x elasticity 0.5 -> +1.7% volume -> EBITDA +5.8% -> x1.04 x0.5 -> +3.0; shaded.
Industrial/warehousing/data-centre construction ~7% of demand; +10% capex growth -> +0.5% volume -> +1.9% EBITDA -> +1.0; rounded +1.2.

Interest cost small (Rs552 cr in Q2 vs EBITDA Rs3,719 cr). +25bp on gross debt of ~Rs15-16k cr (model estimate) -> -Rs40 cr, -0.8% PBT. Plus P/E 40.6 duration: ~-1.5% for +25bp on long-duration equity, partly offset. Net -1.0. RBI hiked to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, stance 'calibrated tightening' (Reuters/The Hindu/Moneycontrol headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Heavy monsoon delays site work in Q2/Q3; rural income benefit later. Slightly negative.
Housing support (subvention, PMAY) lifts IHB demand: +1 SSU ~ +0.7% volume -> +3.5% EBITDA -> x1.04 x0.5 = +1.8.
Limestone royalty/DMF increases raise raw-material cost (~14% of costs); partly passed on with long lags.

supply_chain.note: ~56% holder (model knowledge); GRASIM trades on look-through value

company_events.event: Industry price hikes of Rs12-15/bag realised
Q3 FY27 results (UltraTech usually reports mid/late Jan; estimate)
Capacity commissioning towards 240 MT (timeline of 240 MT target not verified)

current_state.trend: Revenue +19% y/y on volumes; OPM 16.0% (vs 15.8% y/y, 20.4% in Q1); PAT +21% but -42% q/q. TTM sales Rs95,572 cr, OP Rs18,244 cr, PAT Rs8,835 cr.
current_state.valuation: P/E 40.6, P/B 4.9; EV/EBITDA ~19x TTM (derived). Rich vs history on depressed margins; stock +13.9% in 1m after Q2.
